comparator.name: Medische Natuurwetenschappen
comparator.sourceNotes: The Dutch full-time VU Medische Natuurwetenschappen bachelor has no formal specialisations. The adopted 2026–2027 OER Article 11.3 gives twelve credited Year-1 units (60 EC), eleven Year-2 units (60 EC), an 18 EC individual bachelor project, a 6 EC science/society/history unit and one 6 EC restricted choice, plus 30 EC open study: 180 EC in 27 components. The restricted options are Machine Learning, Computational (Pharmaco)Chemistry and Project systeemmodelleren. None is an official route or uniquely more general in the formal evidence; the first-listed Machine Learning is the neutral tie-break, selected before reassessing UCR fit. The previous claim that the systems project is uniquely representative because of its name and systems-biology connection is withdrawn: its actual content is physical system/signal theory and ECG measurement. Recruitment lists some predecessor units separately; the adopted combined units control, with transitions in Article 15.2, not duplicate credits. The Dutch diagnostic test or completed refresher gates Inleiding MNW en mentoraat; lab safety gates Practicum 1 and zero-credit Study and Career gates Practicum 2. These add no credits. BSA normally requires 42 first-year EC. Thesis entry under Article 9.1 requires Year 1 and Year 2 completion with at most 12 EC deficiency, excluding practicals; the annual project description additionally expects in principle all other non-elective components completed. The project is individual, includes a literature study, theoretical/experimental work and data analysis, and is assessed as work 50%, written report 40%, presentation 10%. The coherent pathway completes the major and selected choice before the project; no future dated offering is guaranteed. Practicum 2 continues the combined first-year physics/programming practical; its annual prerequisite still names predecessor X_430105, reconciled through Article 15.2 and the current course description. Open study permits a minor, individual academic units, study abroad or an internship, normally with prior examination-board permission; individual/foreign selections include at least 12 EC level 300 and at most 6 EC level 100. Study abroad may include one 6 EC master unit not reused in a subsequent master. Eligible university minors and six listed minors have approval exemptions. Practical/tutorial attendance may be required by individual manuals. Honours are extra. The optional NVKF certificate requires a specified biomedical-imaging minor, bioinformatics/systems biology, systems project or machine learning, a physical/biomedical-physical thesis and the relevant master requirements; it is not an automatic clinical-physicist qualification or a compulsory route of this generic comparator.

components.note: Capstone project studying how cancer arises and how it is diagnosed and treated.

components.name: Vrije keuzeruimte (minor, free choice of units, study abroad, or internship)
components.note: Genuine open profiling space of at least 30 EC in semester 1 of year 3 (OER Article 12.1): a programmed minor (six approved options including Biomedische Beeldvorming and Neurosciences), a free individual choice of units of education (at least 12 EC at level 300, at most 6 EC at level 100), study abroad, or an internship. Preserved as open space rather than instantiated with invented content.

programmes.label: Medische Natuurwetenschappen at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam

exception.reason: The strongest proposed UCR programme is coherent and feasible, with 12 biomedical courses (90 EC), 10 mathematics/computing courses (75 EC), introductory research methods (7.5 EC) and mandatory PPD (7.5 EC). Its substantial physiology, biochemical/molecular disease study, molecular laboratory work and quantitative/image-analysis contributions are preserved. They do not implement the defining integration of experimental medical physics, physical chemistry and physiological measurement in this degree. VU physics practicals combine experiments, error analysis and Python/MATLAB; later work includes ultrasound/interferometry and physical measurement models. Optics treats wave propagation, interference, diffraction and lasers; radiation/audiology uses physical models; quantum-to-molecule study links microscopic theory and spectroscopy to medical applications. Clinical analytical chemistry teaches extraction, chromatography, spectroscopy and mass spectrometry. UCR image processing explicitly includes medical applications, but processing an image is not the physics of acquiring it. Its machine learning, database and neural-network courses do not supply molecular-network dynamics, sequence/transcriptomics analysis or measured physiological signal modelling. Life Science Laboratory has genuine PCR, ELISA, protein and introductory bioinformatics work, not a substitute for the physical measurement/analytical-chemistry sequence. A reconstruction from actual sustainability content was tested: Sustainability Essentials introduces physics/chemistry in planetary-boundary problems and R3 includes inorganic chemistry and resource-recovery laboratory skills. Those are real contributions, so the prior statement that UCR has no physics or chemistry at all is false; their purpose and progression do not remedy the missing medical-physical/analytical sequence. Reweighting the same biomedical and data courses would change the organising inquiry to biomedical or health-data science. No complete substantive UCR response to this integrated target is established; this is not based merely on a degree title, professional licence, an absent individual course, or a matching quota.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Medical Natural Sciences brings physics, chemistry, mathematics and computing together with physiology to investigate disease and medical technology. Students learn experimental measurement, molecular analysis and modelling before completing an individual research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers substantial biomedical science, molecular laboratory work, mathematics and image/data analysis. The available courses do not establish a complete programme organised around the physical and chemical principles of medical measurement and technology. We therefore show the verified VU curriculum without presenting a UCR programme as a comparable alternative.

curriculum.routeLabel: Common major; Machine Learning selected from the compulsory choice
curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC pathway contains 60 EC in each year, including 30 EC open study and an 18 EC individual research project. The restricted 6 EC choice is not a specialisation. Language, lab-safety and career-study requirements add no credits; project entry, elective-level and approval conditions apply. Clinical-physics certification and training have additional requirements.
